Summary
Jack Beckerman, stationed in Brisbane, shares updates on his work, health, and social life. He mentions receiving an anniversary letter and discusses his recent budget preparation, which involves significant financial computations. He also shares photographs of his office and expresses his desire to move out of the area before feeling like a native. He expresses hope that the photos and letters he sends give a better picture of life in Brisbane. He also mentions his social work and family updates, including his parents' health and his own movie-going habits.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_18a) --- Dear Folks and Ruth: Received your "anniversary" letter of 22 Feb 1945 a few days ago. Work has been coming in rather slow lately. I've been under the pressure of recently preparing budget for the theater! (Happens every 3 mos.) Considering that computations involve considerable millions of dollars it's rather a nerve racking job. A lucky break is me - a friend of mine gave me 6 pictures he took of our old office in W'Whitner Bldg. It will give you a good picture of the place. Nos. 1 and 2 show the machine bookkeeping machine we use in our section. Remember the letter I typed on one of them. Nos. 3 & 4 show cross views of about 1/4th of the entire office. Nos. 5 & 6 are snaps of "my" section of the place. The do one [illegible] entrance to the machine bookkeeping room. These are good shots to add to the collection. --- Page 2 (Beckerman_18b) --- One contains a "civilian" list of the 160 soldiers that work here. It looks rather odd without the "pl" "Sgt" prefix. Now here rather slim. Feeling no peak of health & good spirits. I hope you're enjoying all this "junk" I've been sending with my letters. Think it tends to give you a better picture of what life here is like. I really wanted like to move out of here before I get to feel like a native. Already I know almost every street and body around Brisbane. Have many friends - interesting companions (including the young ladies). Things are just a little too comfortable. Live in large single rooms maid service, I bought a lovely radio several months ago (gets short in the states) spend wave for eat mi and spare moments. They even deliver beer to any door every week - just like the milkman. That's the war I'm fighting. --- Page 3 (Beckerman_18c) --- 3. Glad to hear that you're getting on with your social work, Ruth. It certainly looks like a lucrative future for you. Since uptown city is a pleasant change from the crowded downtown school. There must be plenty of part-time work in your field! So go at it. How's Mom getting along? So I've become a movie-goer. Hope I'll be getting a chance to join you are of these days. And Pappa is good health. That's wonderful. I'm off for a good night's sleep. We're hitting our cool weather now. The kind that makes you feel like taking some time to make yourself more comfortable. Good night, Mom. I love to you all, Jack.
